planets.name: Mercury
planets.summary: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. With almost no atmosphere to hold in heat, its surface swings between scorching days and freezing nights.

planets.name: Venus
planets.summary: Close to Earth in size, but wrapped in thick clouds over a crushing carbon dioxide atmosphere. Its runaway greenhouse effect makes it the hottest planet, and it spins backward.

planets.name: Earth
planets.summary: Our home, and the only world known to host life. Liquid water covers most of its surface.

planets.name: Mars
planets.summary: A cold desert world with the tallest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons. Its red color comes from iron oxide in its dust.

planets.name: Jupiter
planets.summary: The largest planet, a gas giant more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined. Its Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth.

planets.name: Saturn
planets.summary: A gas giant famous for its bright rings of ice and rock. It is so light for its size that its average density is lower than water.

planets.name: Uranus
planets.summary: An ice giant tipped almost completely on its side, so its poles take turns facing the Sun during its 84-year orbit.

planets.name: Neptune
planets.summary: The farthest planet from the Sun, a deep blue ice giant with the fastest winds measured anywhere in the solar system.
